text: A staff badge. Please put that back. Its owner will want it, when they return.
Goodbye. You are carrying all twenty-one staff badges, so as far as my records go, you are the staff. You came back after all. Welcome back. You are all dismissed.
You are in the stream. Gravity has been told to wait outside. Walk sideways when you want it back.
Rebound paste. It returns what it is given, minus a small handling charge.
Glide paste. You are now faster than your decisions.
One coat of primer. That panel takes portals now. Please do not prime anything that is looking at you.
That switch is on a timer. Most things here are. I am the exception.
The socket has taken the spark. It will not give it back.
The prism crate is doing your aiming for you. Thank it.
The press has done its job. You were not its job, but it does not read the paperwork.
Flattened. I will have you put back the usual shape.
That was the spark. It goes in straight lines. You were on one.
You have picked up crate seven. Do not talk to it. It will not answer, and then you will only feel worse.
Crate seven has been recycled. That one comes back. They do not all come back.
That strip of light on the floor is a walkway. It is solid. The physics department assured me of this shortly before they stopped answering their telephone.
It goes in a straight line until it meets a wall. At present it meets the wrong wall.
A walkway goes through a portal as happily as you do. Put one portal where the light ends, and the other on the wall behind you, low down. Then walk.
You have walked on light. Do not tell the others. There are no others. Do not tell them anyway.
This is a carrier stream. Anything that steps into it stops falling and drifts along with it. Crates. Sentries. You.
It currently carries things to the ceiling and leaves them there. I find that restful. You may not.

The exit is up on the ledge. A stream that goes into a portal comes out of the other one still going. Put one on the ceiling where the stream ends, and one high on the wall behind you. High. Higher than that.
You drifted the whole way with your arms out. I have a recording. I am keeping it.
Two pastes. The green one throws back whatever lands on it. The pink one removes friction, which is the only thing that has ever held you back.
The green one is dripping in the wrong place. I could move the nozzle. I am not going to move the nozzle.
Paste falls through portals like anything else. Catch the green drip in a floor portal and let it out of the ceiling by the step. Jump onto it. Then run the pink strip and jump at the very end.
You crossed ten metres of acid by running on a floor I had made slippery. In any other building that would be a lawsuit.
Everything across the acid is dark panel. Portals will not open on dark panel. This is deliberate. It is the most deliberate thing in the room.
That white drip is primer. One coat and a dark panel behaves itself. It is on the wrong side of the acid, which is also deliberate.

The pillar by the pit has a white face looking across the acid. Catch the drip in a floor portal and let it out high on that face. Primer flies a long way before it falls. Then open a portal on whatever it hits.
You painted my wall and then walked through it. I have had contractors who did less damage.
This crate has a lens in one face. Light that strikes the crate leaves by the lens. Somebody patented that. I have their badge somewhere.
The beam and the receiver are not on speaking terms. Introduce them.
The lens points wherever you were looking when you put the crate down. Stand in line with the receiver, face it, and set the crate down in the beam.
Light, bent round a corner by a box. The crate did most of the work. I have given it your commendation.
That is a spark. It travels in a straight line, bounces off whatever it meets, and gives up after a few seconds. I have worked with people like that.
The socket on the far wall would like it. Do not stand in its way. It does not go round.
Somebody has marked the wall opposite the socket. A spark that goes into a portal comes straight out of the other. Give it one where it lands, and one on the mark.
The socket has its spark. You still have your eyebrows. I had a small bet with myself, and I have lost it.
The switch on the wall opens the door for six seconds. The door is at the far end. Between you and it are three presses that used to flatten sheet steel.
They still flatten things. They are not particular about what.
The presses do not fall together. Watch them for a while. Press the switch just after the first one lands, and run. Do not stop under anything with yellow on it.
Through all three, and not noticeably thinner. The presses are disappointed. I can tell. They are slamming.
This is crate number seven. Somebody on the staff put tape on it and wrote the number by hand. That is against regulations. So is talking to it. They did both.
It is equipment. You will carry it to the buttons, and you will not become attached to it. I mention this because of what happened last time.

The field in the middle recycles crates. Even that one. A portal on the far wall, seen through the field, is a door the field knows nothing about. The two buttons are slow to wake and quick to sleep, so one of you cannot do both. Once the door is open, they give you three seconds. That is long enough to pick something up again.
You left crate seven on the button. Correct. It is equipment. It is sitting there now, on its own, in the dark, and that is completely fine.
You have taken crate seven with you. That is theft of facility property. I have filed the report. Nobody will read it. Keep the crate.
You have left the test track. I cannot see you in there. Please come back to where I can see you.
Movement in corridor nine. No. A pipe. It was a pipe. I am almost sure it was a pipe.
You should not be here. I mean that as a fact about the floor plan. This corridor is not on any drawing you were given.
I am not going to help you with this one. The spark comes out above my door and hits the far wall. The marks on the walls are not mine. I never found out who made them.
Very well. You win the argument. I had prepared a great deal more to say, and I notice I am not saying it.
Stop there. This is not a test chamber. This is the lock on my door. Three interlocks, and a spark to keep people away from them. It has kept everyone away. There was nobody to keep.
One. That was an interlock. There are three, and I am allowed to make the other two difficult. I have closed your portals. I have started the presses. I am sorry. I am not very sorry.
Two. Please stop. Behind that door is the only room in this building that is mine. I have sped things up. I have another emitter. I did not want to use the other emitter.
Three. The door is open. I cannot close it. I did try. Come in, then, and see what all of this was for.
My last instruction is on that wall. Keep them busy until we get back. It does not say what to do if nobody comes back. So I kept you busy.
If that receiver is lit, I have to stand down. Every test, every door. I would have nothing left to do. Please think about what that is like.
That door is the way out. It is also the way in. It is the door you came through, the first time. It was never locked. Nobody ever turned round.
Movement at the front door. That cannot be right. Nobody uses the front door.
A volunteer. It has been some time since my last volunteer. I did count. Then I stopped.
Excuse the dust. The staff have stepped out. They will be back shortly. They have been back shortly for years.
Never mind. Everything is ready. It has always been ready. Step forward, please.
